739	    def generate_checklist_with_dependencies(self, version, payload, dependencies):
740	        # Read-only dependency-aware checklist generation: the template is
741	        # filtered by the release's change categories exactly like
742	        # generate_checklist, then every direct and indirect prerequisite of
743	        # the selected items is added even when its own categories do not
744	        # apply. The whole dependency graph is validated against the whole
745	        # template first, so edges of template items the filter would drop
746	        # still have to be legal and acyclic. Nothing is written and the
747	        # passed objects are never mutated.
748	        if not isinstance(version, str) or not re.fullmatch(VERSION_PATTERN, version):
749	            raise ValueError("version must have three nonnegative numeric components")
750	        items = self._validated_template(payload)
751	        # Every id in the dependency map, at either end, must reference a
752	        # template item: the complete map and the complete template are
753	        # validated, including items the category filter never selects.
754	        prerequisites = self._validated_dependencies(
755	            dependencies, {item["id"] for item in items})
756	        # The whole store is validated before the version is looked up.
757	        records = self._read_store()
758	        if version not in records:
759	            raise ValueError("unknown release")
760	        selected = self._applicable_template_items(items, records[version])
761	        selected_ids = {item["id"] for item in selected}
762	        # Close over every direct and indirect prerequisite of the selected
763	        # items; shared prerequisites are collected once. Only the member set
764	        # matters here: the final order always follows the template.
765	        closure = set(selected_ids)
766	        pending = list(selected_ids)
767	        while pending:
768	            node = pending.pop()
769	            for prerequisite in prerequisites.get(node, ()):
770	                if prerequisite not in closure:
771	                    closure.add(prerequisite)
772	                    pending.append(prerequisite)
773	        selected_by_id = {item["id"]: item for item in selected}
774	        # Final items keep template order: initially selected items stay in
775	        # their positions and prerequisites added solely for the closure slot
776	        # in at their template positions, even when their categories do not
777	        # apply. The selected dicts already carry the uniform pending item
778	        # shape; added prerequisites are rendered from their template entry.
779	        result_items, dependency_pairs = [], []
780	        for item in items:
781	            item_id = item["id"]
782	            if item_id not in closure:
783	                continue
784	            if item_id in selected_ids:
785	                result_items.append(dict(selected_by_id[item_id]))
786	            else:
787	                result_items.append({"id": item_id, "text": item["text"],
788	                                     "required": item["required"], "status": "pending"})
789	            # Every final id gets a normalized array in template order;
790	            # omitted items and declared empty arrays both freeze to [].
791	            dependency_pairs.append((item_id, list(prerequisites.get(item_id, ()))))
792	        # includedPrerequisites lists, in template order, only the items
793	        # added solely because of a dependency edge.
794	        included_prerequisites = [item["id"] for item in items
795	                                  if item["id"] in closure and item["id"] not in selected_ids]
796	        return {"version": version, "items": result_items,
797	                "dependencies": dict(dependency_pairs),
798	                "includedPrerequisites": included_prerequisites}

815	    def _audit_report(version, items, expected_items):
816	        # Build the audit_checklist report from normalized actual items and the
817	        # expected item set (already filtered/closed over), both sequences of
818	        # four-field items with a pending status on the expected side.
819	        groups = {"done": [], "pending": [], "blocked": []}
820	        ready = True
821	        for item in items:
822	            groups[item["status"]].append(
823	                {"id": item["id"], "text": item["text"],
824	                 "required": item["required"], "status": item["status"]}
825	            )
826	            if item["required"] and item["status"] != "done":
827	                ready = False

829	        actual_by_id = {item["id"]: item for item in items}
830	        expected_ids = set()

832	        for expected in expected_items:
833	            expected_ids.add(expected["id"])
834	            actual = actual_by_id.get(expected["id"])
835	            if actual is None:
836	                missing.append({"id": expected["id"], "text": expected["text"],
837	                                "required": expected["required"], "status": "pending"})
838	            elif actual["text"] != expected["text"] or actual["required"] != expected["required"]:
839	                mismatched.append({
840	                    "expected": {"id": expected["id"], "text": expected["text"],
841	                                 "required": expected["required"], "status": "pending"},
842	                    "actual": {"id": actual["id"], "text": actual["text"],
843	                               "required": actual["required"], "status": actual["status"]}})
844	            else:
845	                if expected["required"] and actual["status"] != "done":
846	                    ready = False
847	                continue
848	            # Differences in optional template items never affect readiness.
849	            if expected["required"]:
850	                ready = False
851	        unexpected = [
852	            {"id": item["id"], "text": item["text"],

854	            for item in items if item["id"] not in expected_ids
855	        ]
856	        return {"version": version, "ready": ready,
857	                "done": groups["done"], "pending": groups["pending"], "blocked": groups["blocked"],

924	    @staticmethod
925	    def _audit_dependency_report(version, items, expected_items, prerequisites, closure):
926	        # Dependency report over the final expected set: actual checklist items
927	        # first in checklist order, then expected items absent from the
928	        # checklist in template order. Actual items keep their definition and
929	        # declared status; appended items take the template definition with a
930	        # pending status. Only dependency edges whose both ends lie in the final
931	        # set count; actual items outside it behave as having no prerequisites.
932	        actual_by_id = {item["id"]: item for item in items}
933	        missing_expected = [expected for expected in expected_items
934	                            if expected["id"] not in actual_by_id]
935	
936	        def declared_status(node):
937	            actual = actual_by_id.get(node)
938	            return actual["status"] if actual is not None else "pending"
939	
940	        effective = {}
941	
942	        def effective_status(node):
943	            # The same memoized effective-status rule as check_dependencies,
944	            # over the final set: an actual item outside the set has no edges.
945	            if node not in effective:
946	                status = declared_status(node)
947	                if node in closure and any(
948	                        effective_status(prerequisite) != "done"
949	                        for prerequisite in prerequisites.get(node, ())
950	                        if prerequisite in closure):
951	                    status = "blocked"
952	                effective[node] = status
953	            return effective[node]
954	
955	        result_items, ready = [], True
956	
957	        def add_report_item(item_id, text, required, declared):
958	            waiting = []
959	            if item_id in closure:
960	                waiting = [prerequisite for prerequisite in prerequisites.get(item_id, ())
961	                           if prerequisite in closure
962	                           and effective_status(prerequisite) != "done"]
963	            effect = effective_status(item_id)
964	            result_items.append({"id": item_id, "text": text, "required": required,
965	                                 "status": declared, "effectiveStatus": effect,
966	                                 "waiting": waiting})
967	            return effect
968	
969	        for item in items:
970	            effect = add_report_item(item["id"], item["text"], item["required"], item["status"])
971	            if item["required"] and effect != "done":
972	                ready = False
973	        for expected in missing_expected:
974	            effect = add_report_item(expected["id"], expected["text"],
975	                                     expected["required"], "pending")
976	            if expected["required"] and effect != "done":
977	                ready = False
978	        return {"version": version, "ready": ready, "items": result_items}

980	    def release_record(self, version, checklist, template, rollback):
981	        # Read-only release snapshot: the audit follows the existing
982	        # audit_checklist rules exactly, and a not-ready audit rejects the
983	        # record without adding any optional-item blocking of its own. The
984	        # returned snapshot is detached from every passed object and carries
985	        # no generated timestamp, so identical inputs yield identical records.
986	        audit = self.audit_checklist(version, checklist, template)
987	        if not audit["ready"]:

    def update_checklist(self, version, updates, checklist_path):
        # Batch-update the statuses of a local checklist file after confirming
        # every expected status still matches the read bytes: one mismatch
        # rejects the whole batch. Only when at least one status changes is the
        # target replaced wholesale with UTF-8 JSON ending in a newline;
        # otherwise its bytes and modification time are left untouched.
        normalized_updates, items, path = self._prepare_checklist_update(
            version, updates, checklist_path)
        status_by_id = {item["id"]: item["status"] for item in items}
        # Ids match case-sensitively after trimming, without Unicode
        # normalization; every expected status is checked, including entries
        # whose target status would not change anything.
        for item_id, expected, _status in normalized_updates:
            actual = status_by_id.get(item_id)
            if actual is None:
                raise ValueError("update item id must exist in the checklist")
            if actual != expected:
                raise ValueError("update expected status does not match the checklist")
        updated, resulting = self._apply_checklist_updates(items, normalized_updates)
        changed = bool(updated)
        if changed:
            content = json.dumps({"version": version, "items": resulting},
                                 ensure_ascii=False, indent=2) + "\n"
            _atomic_write(path, content)
        ready = all(item["status"] == "done" for item in resulting if item["required"])
        return {"version": version, "changed": changed, "items": resulting,
                "updated": updated, "ready": ready}

    def preview_update_checklist(self, version, updates, checklist_path):
        # Read-only plan for update_checklist: the same public validation,
        # store and checklist checks and the same id matching, but unknown ids
        # and expected-status mismatches are reported as conflicts in updates
        # order instead of raised, and nothing is ever written.
        normalized_updates, items, _path = self._prepare_checklist_update(
            version, updates, checklist_path)
        status_by_id = {item["id"]: item["status"] for item in items}
        # Every expected status is checked, including entries whose target
        # status is already satisfied; conflicts keep the updates-array order.
        conflicts = []
        for item_id, expected, target in normalized_updates:
            actual = status_by_id.get(item_id)
            if actual is None:
                conflicts.append({"id": item_id, "expected": expected, "actual": None,
                                  "status": target, "reason": "unknown-id"})
            elif actual != expected:
                conflicts.append({"id": item_id, "expected": expected, "actual": actual,
                                  "status": target, "reason": "status-mismatch"})
        if conflicts:
            # A conflicting batch plans nothing: the normalized original
            # checklist is reported without any partial status changes.
            can_update = False
            resulting = [dict(item) for item in items]
            updated = []
            changed = False
        else:
            can_update = True
            updated, resulting = self._apply_checklist_updates(items, normalized_updates)
            changed = bool(updated)
        ready = all(item["status"] == "done" for item in resulting if item["required"])
        return {"version": version, "canUpdate": can_update, "changed": changed,
                "items": resulting, "updated": updated, "ready": ready,
                "conflicts": conflicts}

    def preview_merge_checklist(self, version, base, incoming, current):
        # Read-only three-way merge preview of same-version checklists: items
        # are matched by normalized id and compared as whole normalized items
        # (id, text, required, status; extra fields ignored, missing differing
        # from any present item). An incoming side equal to the base or to the
        # current side keeps the current side; otherwise a current side equal
        # to the base adopts the incoming side; anything else is one whole-item
        # conflict that keeps the current presence state and content.
        base_items, incoming_items, current_items = self._prepared_merge_inputs(
            version, base, incoming, current)
        merged, conflicts = self._merge_classification(
            base_items, incoming_items, current_items)
        items = self._ordered_merge_items(merged, incoming_items, current_items)
        self._validate_merge_items(items)
        ready = all(item["status"] == "done" for item in items if item["required"])

    def resolve_merge_checklist(self, version, base, incoming, current, decisions):
        # Read-only confirmation layer over preview_merge_checklist: decisions
        # maps original preview conflict ids to "incoming" or "current"; empty
        # and partial maps are allowed. A chosen side is adopted as one whole
        # item and choosing a side that lacks the id deletes the item.
        # Unchosen conflicts keep their original details and the current side.
        if not isinstance(version, str) or not re.fullmatch(VERSION_PATTERN, version):
            raise ValueError("version must have three nonnegative numeric components")
        base_items = self._validated_checklist(base, version)
        incoming_items = self._validated_checklist(incoming, version)
        current_items = self._validated_checklist(current, version)
        choices = _validated_merge_choices(decisions)
        # The whole store is validated before the version is looked up; a
        # missing store is treated as empty and then reports it as unknown.
        records = self._read_store()
        if version not in records:
            raise ValueError("unknown release")
        merged, conflicts = self._merge_classification(
            base_items, incoming_items, current_items)
        # The original preview must itself stay a legal checklist before any
        # decision is applied.
        self._validate_merge_items(
            self._ordered_merge_items(merged, incoming_items, current_items))
        conflict_ids = {entry["id"] for entry in conflicts}
        # Keys match the normalized conflict ids exactly: case-sensitive, with
        # no trimming or Unicode normalization, and never at a non-conflict id.
        for item_id in choices:
            if item_id not in conflict_ids:
                raise ValueError("decision id is not a conflict id")
        resolved = [{"id": item_id, "choice": choice}

        # Apply the confirmed whole-item choices over the preview plan. A side
        # lacking the id deletes the item; building from deep copies keeps
        # every passed object untouched, and confirming an unchanged current
        # side still counts as resolved.
        incoming_by_id = {item["id"]: item for item in incoming_items}

        items = self._ordered_merge_items(merged, incoming_items, current_items)
        self._validate_merge_items(items)
        remaining = [entry for entry in conflicts if entry["id"] not in chosen_by_id]
        ready = all(item["status"] == "done" for item in items if item["required"])
        # Ids sort by Unicode code point, not by locale.

        resolved.sort(key=lambda entry: entry["id"])
        return {"version": version, "canMerge": not remaining, "ready": ready,

            self.resolve(base, target, current, {"/db/port": custom})
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
            self.resolve({"a": 1}, {"a": 2}, {"a": 3}, {"/b": custom})

    def test_invalid_custom_decision_objects(self):
        base, target, current = {"a": 1}, {"a": 2}, {"a": 3}
        invalid_objects = (
            {},
            {"value": 1},
            {"present": True},
            {"present": False, "value": 1},
            {"present": 1},
            {"present": 0},
            {"present": "true"},
            {"present": None},
            {"present": True, "value": 1, "extra": 2},
            {"present": False, "extra": 2},
            {"present": True, "value": float("nan")},
            {"present": True, "value": float("inf")},
            {"present": True, "value": object()},
            {"present": True, "value": {1: 2}},
            {"present": True, "value": [float("-inf")]},
            {"present": True, "value": {"k": {"n": object()}}},
        )
        for choice in invalid_objects:
            with self.assertRaises(ValueError, msg=choice):
                self.resolve(base, target, current, {"/a": choice})
        cycle = {"x": 1}
        cycle["self"] = cycle
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
            self.resolve(base, target, current, {"/a": {"present": True, "value": cycle}})

        snapshot = json.loads(json.dumps(decisions))
        result = self.resolve(base, target, current, decisions)
        self.assertEqual(decisions, snapshot)
        # Mutating the returned config never reaches the decisions object.
        result["config"]["a"]["nested"].append(3)
        self.assertEqual(decisions["/a"]["value"], {"nested": [1, 2]})
        # Mutating the input after the call never reaches the result.
        decisions["/a"]["value"]["nested"].append(99)
        self.assertEqual(result["config"]["a"]["nested"], [1, 2, 3])

                                             ("9.9.9", "1.0.0"), ("1.0.0", "9.9.9")):

        reverse = self.resolve({"a": 2}, {"a": 1}, {"a": 3}, {"/a": "current"}, "2.0.0", "1.0.0")
        self.assertEqual(reverse["config"], {"a": 3})

    def test_readonly_inputs_store_untouched_and_results_detached(self):
        before, mtime = self.path.read_bytes(), self.path.stat().st_mtime_ns
        base = {"port": 80, "gone": {"a": [1]}}
        target = {"port": 8080, "gone": {"a": [2]}}
        current = {"port": 9000, "gone": {"a": [3]}}

        snapshots = [json.loads(json.dumps(payload)) for payload in (base, target, current)]
        result = self.resolve(base, target, current, dict(decisions))
        self.assertTrue(result["canApply"])
        self.assertEqual(base, snapshots[0])

            path.write_text(json.dumps(payload), encoding="utf-8")

        store_before = self.path.read_bytes()

            self.command("1.2.0", *paths, str(self.current)),

        # Reapplying against the new snapshot with no leftover decisions is a

        # Read-only confirmation layer over preview_merge_checklist: decisions
        # maps original preview conflict ids to "incoming" or "current"; empty
        # and partial maps are allowed. A chosen side is adopted as one whole
        # item and choosing a side that lacks the id deletes the item.
        # Unchosen conflicts keep their original details and the current side.
        if not isinstance(version, str) or not re.fullmatch(VERSION_PATTERN, version):
            raise ValueError("version must have three nonnegative numeric components")
        base_items = self._validated_checklist(base, version)
        incoming_items = self._validated_checklist(incoming, version)
        current_items = self._validated_checklist(current, version)
        choices = _validated_merge_choices(decisions)
        # The whole store is validated before the version is looked up; a
        # missing store is treated as empty and then reports it as unknown.
        records = self._read_store()
        if version not in records:
            raise ValueError("unknown release")
        merged, conflicts = self._merge_classification(
            base_items, incoming_items, current_items)
        # The original preview must itself stay a legal checklist before any
        # decision is applied.
        self._validate_merge_items(
            self._ordered_merge_items(merged, incoming_items, current_items))
        conflict_ids = {entry["id"] for entry in conflicts}
        # Keys match the normalized conflict ids exactly: case-sensitive, with
        # no trimming or Unicode normalization, and never at a non-conflict id.
        for item_id in choices:
            if item_id not in conflict_ids:
                raise ValueError("decision id is not a conflict id")
        resolved = [{"id": item_id, "choice": choice}
                    for item_id, choice in choices.items()]
        # Apply the confirmed whole-item choices over the preview plan. A side
        # lacking the id deletes the item; building from deep copies keeps
        # every passed object untouched, and confirming an unchanged current
        # side still counts as resolved.
        incoming_by_id = {item["id"]: item for item in incoming_items}
        current_by_id = {item["id"]: item for item in current_items}
        chosen_by_id = {entry["id"]: entry["choice"] for entry in resolved}
        for item_id, choice in chosen_by_id.items():
            side = incoming_by_id if choice == "incoming" else current_by_id
            merged[item_id] = copy.deepcopy(side.get(item_id))
        items = self._ordered_merge_items(merged, incoming_items, current_items)
        self._validate_merge_items(items)
        remaining = [entry for entry in conflicts if entry["id"] not in chosen_by_id]
        ready = all(item["status"] == "done" for item in items if item["required"])
        # Ids sort by Unicode code point, not by locale.
        remaining.sort(key=lambda entry: entry["id"])
        resolved.sort(key=lambda entry: entry["id"])

111	`ReleaseDesk.preview_update_checklist(version, updates, checklist_path)` is a read-only dry run of the same batch: it confirms whether the whole batch would be accepted and shows the planned checklist and readiness without writing, and `python3 release_desk.py update-checklist 1.2.0 updates.json checklist.json --dry-run` runs it with the same positional arguments and `--store` selection; omitting the flag keeps the original writing behavior exactly. The preview follows the same public version, store, checklist, update-entry and id-matching rules as `update_checklist`, in the same order — the version must be registered after the whole store is validated (a missing store is treated as empty and then reports the version as unknown), the target must already exist, must not be a symbolic link and must not alias the store or, on the CLI, the updates file (textual aliases and hard links recognized), and non-UTF-8 bytes, JSON syntax errors and repeated object keys at any level are rejected. An empty updates array is a valid preview that still validates the whole store and the whole checklist. Illegal input, an unregistered version, a checklist version mismatch, an invalid store, non-UTF-8 bytes, a JSON syntax error or a repeated key raises `ValueError`; a read failure or a missing target raises `OSError`; neither success nor failure modifies the passed array, the updates file, the checklist file, its modification time or the store, and no file or directory is created.
112	
113	Instead of raising, unknown ids and expected-status mismatches become conflict entries reported in updates-array order: each conflict holds only the normalized `id`, the `expected` status, `actual`, the target `status` and `reason`; `actual` is `null` with reason `unknown-id` for an id absent from the checklist, and `reason` is `status-mismatch` with the read status as `actual` otherwise. A target status that is already satisfied still has its `expected` status checked. The result holds only `version`, `canUpdate`, `changed`, `items`, `updated`, `ready` and `conflicts`, and every array is always present. With no conflicts `canUpdate` is true, `items` keeps the checklist order and normalized four fields changing only matched statuses, `updated` lists, in checklist order, only the ids whose status would actually change, and `changed` is true only when that array is non-empty; `ready` follows the existing rule that every required item is `done`. With any conflict `canUpdate` is false, `items` is the normalized original checklist unchanged, `updated` is empty, `changed` is false and no partial update is reported; `ready` then reflects the original checklist. A valid preview prints the single-line result with exit 0 even when it reports conflicts; any exception prints only a single-line `error` object with exit 2. Other public entry points keep their existing behavior.
114	
115	`ReleaseDesk.preview_merge_checklist(version, base, incoming, current)` is a read-only three-way merge preview of same-version checklists, and `python3 release_desk.py merge-checklist 1.2.0 base.json incoming.json current.json` reads the common base, the incoming checklist and the current checklist from three UTF-8 JSON files in that order using the same `--store` selection. All three inputs follow the existing checklist rules — including the rule that each declared version must equal the queried version — the whole store is validated before the version is looked up (a missing store is treated as empty and then reports the version as unknown), and the version must be registered. Items are matched by their normalized ids, case-sensitively after trimming with no Unicode normalization, and compared as whole normalized items: only `id`, `text`, `required` and `status` take part, extra fields are ignored, and a missing item differs from any present one.
116	
117	For each id, an incoming side equal to the base or to the current side keeps the current side; otherwise a current side equal to the base adopts the incoming side; every remaining case is one whole-item conflict that keeps the current side's presence state and content. Additions, deletions and modifications all follow this rule, non-conflicting changes still enter the preview, and item fields are never merged separately. The result holds only `version`, `canMerge`, `ready`, `items` and `conflicts`: `canMerge` is true only when no conflict was reported, and `ready` follows the existing rule that every required item is `done`. `items` carries only the four normalized fields, keeps the current-side item order and then appends, in incoming-side order, the preview items the current side lacks. `conflicts` is always an array, sorted by id in Unicode code point order, each entry holding only `id`, `base`, `incoming` and `current`, the last three being the complete normalized item or `null` when that side lacks the id. A preview that would be empty or would hold no required item raises `ValueError`, and this result validation applies to conflicting previews too.
118	
119	An invalid or unregistered version, a declared-version mismatch, an invalid checklist or store, an empty preview or a preview without any required item raises `ValueError`, while a missing or unreadable file raises `OSError`; the CLI additionally rejects non-UTF-8 files, JSON syntax errors and repeated object keys at any level in any of the three files, printing only a single-line `error` object with exit 2. A valid preview — conflicts included — prints the single-line result with exit 0. Neither success nor failure modifies the passed payloads, the input files or the store, no file or directory is created, and mutating the returned data never reaches the inputs. Other public entry points keep their existing behavior.

121	`ReleaseDesk.resolve_merge_checklist(version, base, incoming, current, decisions)` is a read-only confirmation layer over `preview_merge_checklist`, and `python3 release_desk.py resolve-merge-checklist 1.2.0 base.json incoming.json current.json decisions.json` reads the three checklists and the decisions from four UTF-8 JSON files in that order using the same `--store` selection. The version, checklist, store and version-registration checks follow `merge-checklist` exactly, including validating the whole store first, treating a missing store as empty and then reporting the version as unknown, matching declared versions, comparing whole normalized items, merging non-conflicting changes identically, and requiring both the original preview and the confirmed checklist to be non-empty and to contain at least one required item.
122	
123	`decisions` is a JSON object, possibly empty, mapping original preview conflict ids to either the string `"incoming"` or the string `"current"`; partial selections are allowed. Keys match the normalized conflict ids exactly — case-sensitively, without trimming surrounding whitespace or Unicode normalization — and a key that is not an original conflict id is rejected, as is any non-object decision value, non-string key or choice other than the two strings. Choosing a side adopts that side's complete item; item fields are never merged separately. When the chosen side lacks the id the item is deleted, and choosing a side whose content is unchanged still counts as a confirmed decision. Unchosen conflicts keep their original details (including the current side's presence state and content) and keep the current item in the checklist; their fields are never merged field by field.
124	
125	The result holds only `version`, `canMerge`, `ready`, `items`, `conflicts` and `resolved`. `items` carries only the four normalized fields, follows the current-side item order and then appends, in incoming-side order, items the current side originally lacked; confirmed deletions are absent. `canMerge` is true only when `conflicts` is empty, and `ready` follows the existing rule that every required item is `done`. `conflicts` holds only the unconfirmed conflicts in the preview structure, and each `resolved` entry holds only `id` and the original `choice` string. Both arrays are always present and are sorted by id in Unicode code point order. An invalid or unregistered version, a declared-version mismatch, an invalid checklist or store, a non-object decisions value, a non-string key, a key that is not an original conflict id, an illegal choice, or an empty or required-item-free original preview or confirmed checklist raises `ValueError`, while a missing or unreadable checklist or decisions file raises `OSError`; the CLI additionally rejects non-UTF-8 files, JSON syntax errors and repeated object keys at any level in any of the four files, printing only a single-line `error` object with exit 2. A valid run prints the single-line result with exit 0 even when conflicts remain. Neither success nor failure modifies the passed objects, the input files or the store, no file or directory is created, and mutating the returned data never reaches the inputs. All other public entry points keep their existing behavior.

127	`ReleaseDesk.apply_merge_checklist(version, base, incoming, expected, decisions, current_path)` saves a confirmed merge to a local checklist file, and `python3 release_desk.py apply-merge-checklist 1.2.0 base.json incoming.json expected.json decisions.json current.json` reads the base, incoming and expected checklists plus the decisions from four UTF-8 JSON files in that order using the same `--store` selection and treats the fifth path as the write target. The version, checklist, decisions, store and version-registration checks follow `resolve-merge-checklist` exactly, with the expected checklist validated like every other checklist. The target file must already exist and must not be a symbolic link, and it must not be the same file as the store or as any of the four input files — textual path aliases and hard links are recognized — with violations raising `ValueError`; a missing target or any read or write failure raises `OSError`, and neither a missing target nor missing directories are ever created. The file is read as UTF-8 JSON under the same whole-file duplicate-key rule as everywhere (encoding, syntax and repeated-key errors raise `ValueError`), validated like any checklist, and its declared version and normalized item sequence must equal the expected snapshot: extra fields, object key order and trimmable surrounding whitespace do not take part, item order does, and any mismatch raises `ValueError` before anything is written. The merge then follows `resolve_merge_checklist` exactly — whole-item merging, incoming/current side selections, deletions, ordering and result legality — with the actually read target as the current side; any conflict left undecided raises `ValueError`, an empty decisions object is valid when there are no conflicts, and a not-ready result still saves. The result holds only `version`, `changed`, `items`, `resolved` and `ready`, where `items` and `resolved` carry the same content and ordering as the corresponding `resolve_merge_checklist` result. `changed` is true only when the normalized item sequence differs from the read one; then the target is replaced wholesale with UTF-8 JSON holding only `version` and `items` and ending in a newline, and when it is false the target's bytes and modification time are left untouched. Validation and read or write failures always preserve the target's original bytes and leave no new file or directory behind, and neither success nor failure modifies the passed objects, the input files or the store; mutating the returned data never reaches the inputs. All other public entry points keep their existing behavior.

input.new_string: `decisions` is a JSON object, possibly empty, mapping original preview conflict ids to either the string `"incoming"`, the string `"current"` or a custom decision object; strings and custom objects may be mixed and partial selections are allowed. Keys match the normalized conflict ids exactly — case-sensitively, without trimming surrounding whitespace or Unicode normalization — and a key that is not an original conflict id is rejected, as is any non-object decision value, non-string key or choice other than the two strings and a legal custom object. Choosing a side adopts that side's complete item; item fields are never merged separately. When the chosen side lacks the id the item is deleted, and choosing a side whose content is unchanged still counts as a confirmed decision. A custom decision has a strict boolean `present` and no other shape: `{"present": true, "value": item}` replaces the whole conflicted item with `item`, and `{"present": false}` deletes it. A present value is one whole item holding exactly `id`, `text`, `required` and `status`, validated and trimmed under the checklist item rules (extra or missing fields, a non-boolean `required` or an illegal status are rejected); the value replaces the whole item and is never merged field by field, and its normalized id must equal the decision key exactly, so a trimmed id that normalizes to the key is accepted while any other normalized id is rejected. Even a custom value equal to one of the sides, or a custom deletion of an item the current side already lacks, is recorded with choice `"custom"`. Unchosen conflicts keep their original details (including the current side's presence state and content) and keep the current item in the checklist; their fields are never merged field by field.

content.text:
Done. Custom entry confirmation is implemented for the ReleaseDesk checklist merge, scoped exactly to `resolve_merge_checklist`, `apply_merge_checklist` and their CLI commands.

## Changes (`release_desk.py`)

**Choice validation** — `_validated_merge_choices` now accepts, alongside `"incoming"`/`"current"`, a strict custom object via new `_validated_custom_merge_choice`:
- `present` must be a real JSON boolean (rejects `1`/`0`/`"true"`/`null`).
- `true`: object contains exactly `present` + `value`; the value is one whole item holding exactly `id`, `text`, `required`, `status`, validated and trimmed by the same checklist rules (new shared helper `_validated_checklist_item`, used by `_validated_checklist` too), and its normalized id must equal the decision key.
- `false`: object contains only `present` (deletion).
- Missing/extra fields, malformed items, and id mismatches raise `ValueError`. Non-conflict keys are still rejected after classification.

**Resolution** — both methods apply custom choices by replacing `merged[id]` wholesale with a deep copy of the normalized value (or `None` to delete); no field-level merge. `resolved` always records `{"id", "choice": "custom"}` for objects, even when the value equals a side or the item was already absent. Strings and objects may be mixed and partially confirmed; unconfirmed conflicts keep the current side and stay in `conflicts`. Ordering (current first, then incoming-only, deletions taking no slot), `canMerge` (remaining conflicts only), `ready` (required items `done`), and the non-empty/has-required legality checks are unchanged. Read-only results stay detached from inputs.

**Write path** — snapshot comparison, symlink/store/input-file protection, unresolved-conflict rejection, not-ready saves allowed, and "normalized sequence unchanged ⇒ keep bytes and mtime" all preserved; failures leave no file/directory behind. CLI still emits one-line JSON with exit 0 / one-line `error` with exit 2.

The merge preview and all other public entry points are untouched. README sections for both commands now document the custom shape, `"custom"` choice, and error cases.

**Verification**: all 397 existing unit tests pass; additional API and CLI checks confirmed custom replace/delete, side-equal-but-custom recording, trimming semantics, mixed/partial decisions, readiness, every invalid structure, byte/mtime preservation, and non-UTF-8/duplicate-key rejection.
